title: A `started` train response with a missing `job_id` is silently surfaced as a completed model instead of failing loudly
description: In handleTrain the dispatch is: `if (result.status === "started" && result.job_id) { startTrainJob(...) } else if (result.status === "error") { completeTrainJob(...) } else { completeTrainJob(...) }`. The `&& result.job_id` guard means a response with `status === "started"` but a falsy/absent `job_id` does NOT register an async job — it falls through to the generic `else` and is stored via `completeTrainJob(nodeId, result as TrainResult)` as though training had finished. `parseTrainResponse` (frontend/src/types/guards.ts:1088-1089) validates `status` against `["started","completed","error"]` but parses `job_id` with `optionalNullableString`, so a `started`-without-`job_id` payload is a *valid* parse result and this branch is reachable. The stored object has no metrics/model_path (training never ran), yet getModellingPreview (useNodeResultsStore.ts:1098-1105) and TrainingActionsAndResults (TrainingActionsAndResults.tsx:202) only special-case `status === "error"`, so a `"started"` result renders the green 'Model trained — results in preview panel below' badge. This masks a backend contract violation instead of failing loudly, contrary to CLAUDE.md ('code should be allowed to fail loudly ... far superior to a fallback which is incorrect and hard to notice'). The correct behaviour is to throw when `status === "started"` and `job_id` is missing.
evidence: Line 140: `if (result.status === "started" && result.job_id)` → async path. Lines 146-149 `else { completeTrainJob(nodeId, result as unknown as TrainResult) }` catches `status==="completed"` AND `status==="started" && !job_id`. guards.ts:1089 `job_id: optionalNullableString(...)` allows null/absent. TrainingActionsAndResults.tsx:202 `trainResult && trainResult.status !== "error" && ...` → renders success badge for a `started` result that has no real output.
